findings.detected_pattern: p = CATALOG.get(sku) followed by p["amount"] with no None check
findings.issue: getPrice() does not handle an unknown SKU. CATALOG.get(sku) returns None, so p["amount"] raises TypeError ('NoneType' object is not subscriptable). total_price() calls getPrice() for every SKU, so one unknown SKU in a basket crashes the whole total with an unclear error instead of a meaningful lookup failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Check for None before indexing. Either raise a descriptive exception (e.g. KeyError/ValueError naming the SKU) or return a documented sentinel, and have total_price() handle it consistently. Example: if p is None: raise KeyError(f"unknown SKU: {sku}"); return p["amount"].

findings.detected_pattern: p["amount"] on CATALOG.get(sku) result without None check
findings.issue: getPrice is documented to return the catalogue price for a SKU, but for a SKU not in CATALOG, CATALOG.get returns None and p["amount"] raises an opaque TypeError ('NoneType' object is not subscriptable). total_price passes caller-supplied SKUs straight through, so an unknown SKU crashes the whole total with no clear error. The inline comment acknowledges p is None but the code does not handle it.
findings.suggested_fix: if p is None: raise KeyError(f"unknown SKU: {sku}") before indexing (or return None and have total_price handle it explicitly). Either way, make the unknown-SKU behaviour deliberate and document it in the docstring.
